title.en: Australia news live: two more men charged with murder over Chris Baghsarian kidnapping; Labor tips $3.6bn into pay rises for childcare workers
title.zh: 澳洲新闻直播：两名男子因克里斯·巴格萨里安绑架案被控谋杀；工党为托儿所工人加薪36亿澳元

summary.en: Two more men have been charged with murder in connection with the kidnapping of Chris Baghsarian. Separately, the Labor government has allocated $3.6 billion for pay rises for childcare workers. Meanwhile, a legal dispute involving media personalities over significant sums of money continues.
summary.zh: 两名男子因克里斯·巴格萨里安绑架案被控谋杀。此外，工党政府已拨款36亿澳元用于提高托儿所工人的工资。与此同时，涉及媒体名人巨额金钱的法律纠纷仍在继续。

The shock jock agreed to drop his $85m lawsuit against KIIS FM, in return for a cash payment and $1.5m in advertising contra on ARN’s stations for a new broadcasting venture yet to be announced. The inquiry heard evidence of residents being pressured to relocate, deceived about their rights and fearful of losing their homes and communities. Those allegations are serious, but Labor’s response shows they haven’t taken them seriously … They don’t care what the experts say or what people think. We’ve had to send in the Ombudsman to hold Labor to account before they do irreparable damage. Continue reading...

The love of money, as the Bible warns, can be a root of many evils, driving both crime and relentless disputes. It calls us to reflect on...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻摘要呈现了鲜明的对比：绑架谋杀案的悲剧性后果，与数百万美元的高风险法律纠纷，以及政府为确保基本工人的公平工资所做的努力。正如圣经所警告的，贪财是万恶之根，它既能驱动犯罪，也能引发无休止的争执。这提醒我们反思自己的价值观，以及我们最终的安全感和满足感究竟在哪里。

I hope this doesn’t cost CBS any money!” he joked, as Louis Cato and the Great Big Joy Machine performed the song, titled Linus and Lucy, on air. It was a final dig at the network, which many fans believe cancelled the show due to Colbert’s criticisms of the Trump administration. Continue reading...

Such integrity builds trust and ensures fair dealings for all.
reflection.zh: 即使在轻松愉快的时刻，我们的行为也可能产生实际影响，尤其是在涉及协议和知识产权时。这个故事提醒我们，在看似微小的事情上保持忠实，例如尊重创作权利，反映了对诚信的更广泛承诺。这种诚信能够建立信任并确保所有交易的公平。

title.en: Group planned to attack White House UFC event using snipers and drones, FBI says
title.zh: FBI称，一团伙计划使用狙击手和无人机袭击白宫UFC赛事

summary.en: In newly unsealed court filings, the government says the group allegedly expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centres.
summary.zh: 根据最新解封的法庭文件，政府称该团伙据称表达了对腐败、爱泼斯坦档案和数据中心的不满。

body.en:
The FBI thwarted a plot targeting Sunday's UFC event at the White House and has arrested five men, the US justice department said on Tuesday.

Part of the plan involved striking nearby buildings with explosive-laden drones and firing on "high value targets", prosecutors alleged.

One suspect was arrested in Ohio last week, where investigators reviewed encrypted messages involving other alleged conspirators. Prosecutors said in charging documents they had allegedly "expressed ultra-religious and antigovernment sentiments".

"Allegedly planned attacks were stopped cold," FBI Director Kash Patel posted on social media on Tuesday about the "multi-state operation".

The suspects were identified as Tycen C Proper, 19, the suspect arrested in Ohio, along with Bryan Omar Roa, 24, and Michael Alan Thomas, 32, of California, Daniel K Eskridge, 32, of Missouri and Abraham Hermosillo Alvarez, 31, of Nebraska. They were arrested across the four US states and each have been charged with conspiracy to commit murder, the Department of Justice (DOJ) said in a statement.

By using the drones, the plotters aimed to spark panic and draw the fleeing crowd toward a sniper team, according to the court documents. A "second wave" of attackers was then allegedly supposed to storm the White House gate.

An estimated 4,300 people were present for the invite-only event on the South Lawn - and another 85,000 were able to watch nearby - during the back-to-back fights on Sunday.

Court filings related to Alvarez said the group allegedly eyed potential targets that included US President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Elon Musk, as well as several elected officials - though not all attended the UFC event.

The plot was discovered through Proper. His mother called local authorities late on 10 June - just days before the high-profile event - because she was concerned about his large firearms purchases and what she had seen of his online communication with a group that claimed to be made up of former military members and Christian-based.

The group allegedly wanted to "jumpstart" a revolution by shooting "high-value targets" - identified as wealthy people and politicians - attending the UFC fight. They had specifically discussed "grievances about government corruption, the handling of the Epstein files, data centers taking up all the water in communities, and other government actions," prosecutors said.

Group members stated that they wanted "to protect the United States, which they believed was headed in the wrong direction", an FBI document said.

"Members of the group believed that the United States needed to be torn down so that it could be rebuilt," the document said.

The Bible reminds us that all authority is established by God, calling us to respect the rule of law even as we seek justice. It encourages us to address societal concerns through peaceful and constructive means.

title.en: 'Warning fire went up': Couple on board yacht describe encounter with Russian warship
title.zh: “警告性开火了”：游艇上的夫妇描述与俄罗斯军舰的遭遇

summary.en: A Russian frigate reportedly fired warning shots near a British retired couple's yacht in the English Channel, an incident the couple described as a frightening encounter.
summary.zh: 据报道，一艘俄罗斯护卫舰在英吉利海峡向一对英国退休夫妇的游艇附近发射了警告弹，这对夫妇将此次事件描述为一次令人惊恐的遭遇。

body.en:
Retired British couple Jane and Alan Kelvey spoke to BBC's Newsnight after coming into close contact with Russian frigate the Admiral Grigorovich on Tuesday morning.

"They gave out five blasts on their horn, which means, have you seen us?", explained Jane.

"We immediately turned two degrees to port so that they could see we'd made a deliberate change, of course, which meant we had seen them," she added.

The Russian Defence Ministry said the yacht had been on a "dangerous approach" towards the warship, and its crew fired into its path with rifles after making several attempts to contact it over the radio and after launching warning flares.

The Ministry of Defence has described the encounter as an "isolated incident" and not linked to the seizure of a Russian shadow fleet tanker in the Channel on Sunday.

body.zh: 周二早上，退休的英国夫妇简·凯尔维和艾伦·凯尔维在与俄罗斯格里戈罗维奇海军上将号护卫舰进行了密切接触后，接受了英国广播公司的《新闻之夜》采访。 “他们吹响了五声喇叭，这意味着，你看到我们了吗？”简解释道。 “我们立即向左舷转向两度，这样他们就可以看到我们故意做了改变，当然，这意味着我们已经看到了他们，”她补充道。 俄罗斯国防部表示，这艘游艇当时正以“危险的方式”接近这艘军舰，船员在多次尝试通过无线电联系并发射警告弹后，用步枪向其所在路径开火。 国防部将此次遭遇描述为“孤立事件”，与周日在英吉利海峡扣押一艘俄罗斯影子舰队油轮无关。 冲突后，瑞士警方出动水枪并发射催泪瓦斯驱散反七国集团抗议者。 教皇利奥十四世在访问西班牙期间表示，巴塞罗那标志性的圣家堂是“石头、色彩和光线”的杰作。 两名男子在爆炸中受伤，受轻伤被送往医院。 欧冠决赛后与警方发生冲突，近 800 人被捕。 乔丹和希安·亚当斯在都柏林市中心的梅林广场完成了他们的爱尔兰马拉松挑战。 休·斯科菲尔德从巴黎报道，西欧上空出现了一个热穹，导致五月份气温高于平均水平。 近 60 名消防员扑灭了多尼戈尔镇家族经营企业 Cherrymore Kitchens & Bedrooms 的火灾。 这位 27 岁的歌手的歌曲《Bangaranga》为保加利亚赢得了歌曲比赛中的第一个冠军。 威尔士王妃在癌症治疗后返回海外访问时受到了意大利民众的热烈欢迎。 英国广播公司 (BBC) 的盖伊·赫奇科 (Guy Hedgecoe) 从特内里费岛报道，当地一些当地人担心这艘船的抵达可能会带来健康风险。 加那利群岛特内里费岛的人们告诉 BBC，他们对 MV Hondius 的到来感到担忧。 乌克兰军队发现了这名使用无人机的妇女，并在她试图离开饱受战争蹂躏的村庄时派出无人机来营救她。 BBC 的杰西卡·帕克 (Jessica Parker) 探访普里皮亚特 (Pripyat)，这座城市于 1986 年因附近的切尔诺贝利核电站爆炸而被遗弃。 与巴黎拟议的三年协议旨在阻止移民乘坐小船穿越英吉利海峡。 一位慈善抽奖组织者告诉 BBC 广播四台的 Front Row，他给这幅画的新主人打电话。 这位亲欧盟领导人的蒂萨党赢得了压倒性胜利，结束了维克多·欧尔班 16 年的执政生涯。 当人群听到总理的让步时，拉吉尼·瓦伊迪亚纳坦 (Rajini Vaidyanathan) 在匈牙利议会外进行广播。

reflection.en: Encounters like this remind us how quickly peace can be disrupted by displays of power, leaving individuals feeling vulnerable and afraid. In such moments, the ancient promise to "not fear, for I am with you" offers a steadying presence amidst unsettling circumstances. It encourages us to find strength and help beyond immediate threats.
reflection.zh: 这样的遭遇提醒我们，权力展示如何迅速打破和平，让个人感到脆弱和恐惧。在这样的时刻，“你不要害怕，因为我与你同在”的古老应许，在不安的环境中提供了一份稳定的同在。它鼓励我们在即时威胁之外寻求力量和帮助。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: UK investigating reports Russian warship fired warning shots near yacht in English Channel
title.zh: 英国调查俄罗斯军舰在英吉利海峡向游艇开火示警的报道

summary.en: UK authorities are investigating reports that a Russian warship fired warning shots near a yacht in the English Channel. The yacht reportedly drifted towards the Russian frigate Admiral Grigorovich, which was operating in the area.
summary.zh: 英国当局正在调查有关一艘俄罗斯军舰在英吉利海峡向一艘游艇附近开火示警的报道。据了解，这艘游艇当时漂向了在该海峡执行任务的俄罗斯护卫舰“格里戈罗维奇海军上将号”。

body.en:
A British retired couple who were on a yacht which had warning shots fired near it by a Russian warship in the English Channel on Tuesday have described the "surreal" experience to BBC Newsnight.

Jane and Alan Kelvey were sailing 23 miles off the coast of the Isle of Wight on Tuesday morning when they came into close contact with a Russian frigate, the Admiral Grigorovich.

The warship fired into the UK-registered yacht's path, in what the Ministry of Defence has described as an "isolated incident" and not linked to the seizure of a Russian shadow fleet tanker in the Channel on Sunday.

Jane Kelvey told BBC Newsnight: "[The warship] gave out five blasts on their horn, which means 'have you seen us?'

"We immediately turned two degrees to port so they could see we had made a deliberate change of course, which meant we had seen them.

"Then a minute or so later they gave another five blasts on their horn, immediately followed by four to five small arms fire.

"That wasn't aimed at us - it was warning fire that went up in the air, we believe."

Jane said their yacht, the Bright Future, was "definitely not on a collision course", adding: "As far as we were concerned, it wasn't an incident until the gunfire started."

Alan Kelvey said the gunfire had been "unnecessary", and the couple said a Royal Navy vessel arrived to check on their welfare shortly afterwards.

The couple disputed elements of the Russian Defence Ministry's account, which said the yacht had been on a "dangerous approach" towards the warship.

The ministry said its crew fired into the yacht's path with rifles after making several attempts to contact it over the radio and after launching warning flares.

It also said its sailors had acted in "strict accordance with international shipping regulations", while the MoD said it was investigating the incident.

The BBC understands that the small, motor-less yacht had drifted towards the warship in foggy conditions after setting off from the UK.

British officials believe the Admiral Grigorovich was attempting to signal it was drifting rather than being powered by its engines, therefore making it less manoeuvrable - possibly leading its crew to assess it was more vulnerable to a collision.

An MoD spokesperson told the BBC: "Following attempts to contact a British vessel in the channel, the Grigorovich fired warning shots. These were not aimed at the vessel and were an attempt to prevent a possible collision."

A boat from HMS Tyne, a British patrol vessel, was sent to the yacht to gather details and check on the safety of the crew.

The incident comes days after Royal Marine Commandos intercepted a Russian shadow fleet tanker carrying sanctioned oil in the Channel on Sunday, in the first operation of its kind carried out by the British...
body.zh: 周二早上，在两艘船发生密切接触后，一艘俄罗斯军舰在英吉利海峡向一艘英国注册的游艇附近鸣枪示警。 这起涉及俄罗斯护卫舰格里戈罗维奇海军上将号的事件发生在中午前不久，在怀特岛和诺曼底之间。 BBC新闻了解到，这艘小型无动力游艇从英国出发后，在大雾天气中漂向军舰。 俄罗斯国防部表示，这艘游艇正在“危险地接近”这艘军舰，船员在多次尝试通过无线电联系并发射警告弹后，用步枪向其所在路径开火。 它还表示其水手的行为“严格按照国际航运法规”，而英国国防部则表示正在调查这一事件。 英国当局收到游艇乘客的报告，称俄罗斯船只在约 500 码（457 米）外鸣枪示警——以海上旅行的标准来看，这是一个相对较近的距离。 该事件发生在怀特岛以南约 20 海里（约 23 标准英里）处，位于英国领海之外。 几天前，皇家海军陆战队突击队周日在英吉利海峡拦截了一艘装载受制裁石油的俄罗斯影子舰队油轮，这是英国军方首次开展此类行动。 但据了解，英国官员并不认为这一事件与周日的行动有关，而是将其视为个别事件。 俄罗斯军舰定期通过英吉利海峡，并定期受到皇家海军舰艇的监视。 据了解，这艘被认为卷入周二事件的护卫舰当时受到英国皇家海军默西号的跟踪。 周一，美国海军表示，格里戈罗维奇海军上将号周末被英国皇家海军泰恩号和英国皇家海军默西号追踪，称这是在法国布雷斯特海岸附近发现的“例行行动”。 上周，北约消息人士告诉 BBC verify，莫斯科命令格里戈罗维奇海军上将号护送影子舰队通过英吉利海峡。 据了解，这艘护卫舰已在该地区运行了一段时间，并多次由一艘维修船进行补给。 BBC verify 查看的卫星图像显示，近几个月来，这艘维修船 PM-82 在英吉利海峡和北海之间作业。 北约官员认为，PM-82 向格里戈罗维奇海军上将号运送了食物、水和其他补给品，使其能够长时间在海上停留，并带领俄罗斯护航舰队穿越英吉利海峡。 据报道，四月，这艘护卫舰在皇家海军的监视下护送六艘影子舰队通过水道。 虽然周二的事件...

reflection.zh: 即使是意外的相遇，误解和局势升级的可能性也凸显了持续维护和平的必要性。这起事件提醒我们，要尽力与所有人和平相处，努力在任何可能的情况下缓和紧张局势。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: FBI stop alleged drone attack on the White House UFC fight. Here's what we know
title.zh: 联邦调查局阻止了据称针对白宫UFC比赛的无人机袭击。以下是我们所知

summary.en: FBI Director Kash Patel announced that authorities successfully thwarted alleged drone attacks targeting the White House during a UFC fight.
summary.zh: 联邦调查局局长卡什·帕特尔表示，当局成功阻止了据称针对白宫UFC比赛的无人机袭击计划。

body.en:
US law enforcement officials disrupted a planned attack targeting the UFC cage-fighting show staged at the White House this past weekend, according to newly unsealed court papers.

The alleged plotters, disgruntled with the direction of the country, spoke of flying explosives-laden drones at the site and shooting panicked crowd members as they fled.

The FBI obtained encrypted text messages between roughly 20 participants who shared detailed maps of the area and discussed the need for a "safe house" and escape routes after the attack, the documents show.

It was unclear from the court records how close the would-be attackers came to being able to carry out their plan, which was thwarted last week.

FBI agents learned about the possible threat on June 10, four days before the mixed martial arts extravaganza on the White House's South Lawn.

"Thanks to the rapid action of the FBI, our partners, and the Department of Justice in a multi-state operation, multiple individuals are now in custody and allegedly planned attacks were stopped cold," director Kash Patel said in a post to X on Tuesday.

Five people were arrested from states including Ohio, Missouri and California, a law enforcement official familiar with the matter said.

The official spoke to the Associated Press on the condition of anonymity to discuss information that was not yet public.

Among those arrested was Tycen Proper, a 19-year-old Ohio man whose mother contacted local law enforcement last week with concerns about his firearms purchases and online communications, according to an FBI affidavit filed in the case.

An assistant federal public defender assigned to represent Proper, who is charged with crimes including attempted murder of an officer or employee of the United States, did not immediately return messages seeking comment.

Proper admitted in an interview with law enforcement that he participated in the planning of an attack, according to the affidavit, which says some members of the group began communicating with each other last March through a TikTok group called "Vanguard of the Old".

"The members of the group stated that they wanted to protect the United States, which they believed was headed in the wrong direction," the affidavit says.

"Members of the group believed that the United States needed to be torn down so that it could be rebuilt.

"Some expressed a desire that people who were involved with Jeffrey Epstein should not govern the country."

President Donald Trump was friends with Epstein many years ago, but has said he ended their relationship before the disgraced financier's crimes became known.

While human efforts play a role in security, we can find deeper peace knowing that God is an ever-present help in times of trouble. This allows us to face threats not with panic, but with a quiet confidence.
reflection.zh: 阻止袭击的消息提醒我们，即使在潜在危险的时刻，也有力量和避难所的泉源。虽然人类的努力在安全方面发挥作用，但我们更深层的平安在于知道雅伟是我们在患难中随时的帮助。这使我们能够以平静的信心面对威胁，而非恐慌。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: The US-Iran peace deal may be Donald Trump's gain — and Benjamin Netanyahu's problem
title.zh: 美国与伊朗的和平协议可能是唐纳德·特朗普的胜利——本雅明·内塔尼亚胡的难题

summary.en: Trump is claiming a victory, while Netanyahu faces increasing pressure. Experts suggest the deal might only return the US to its original position.
summary.zh: 特朗普称之为胜利，而内塔尼亚胡则面临越来越大的压力。专家表示，这项协议可能只会让美国回到原点。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump declared victory on his 80th birthday, calling for oil to flow through the Strait of Hormuz after the US and Iran announced an interim agreement to end the war in the Middle East.

The agreement will extend the ceasefire for 60 days, with the Strait of Hormuz anticipated to reopen on Friday.

But while Trump is treating the deal like a win, it might be more about optics than a genuine resolution — with the toughest issues kicked down the road and Israel emerging as the "biggest loser" of the deal, according to some experts.

For Trump, the deal's announcement comes as the midterm elections approach in the US, while his domestic popularity wanes.

Energy and fuel prices have soared in the US following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz — through which roughly a fifth of global oil and a significant portion of gas normally transits.

Trump has pledged the strait would be "completely opened" from Friday — a concrete, sellable achievement he can take into November's midterms.

Trump's approval rating is sitting at 36 per cent, according to the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll, down from 47 per cent when he started his second term in January 2025.

The four-day poll, which closed on Monday and was based on responses from 1,537 people in the US, gathered responses before and after the deal was announced, with his rating ticking up a percentage point.

Just 24 per cent of Americans currently approve of his handling of the cost of living.

But Bernard Hourcade, a specialist on Iran at France's CNRS research institute, told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency that the deal for the US was "perhaps a media victory, but not a political victory" and that the US had lost global "credibility" through the conflict.

David Smith, associate professor at the University of Sydney's United States Studies Centre, said the peace deal is an "improvement on the current situation", but stopped short of calling it a win.

"It doesn't get the US any more than they had before the war began," Smith told SBS News. "This deal will be an improvement on the current situation for the US, but overall, the US is worse off than they were before the war began."

That's because Iran has demonstrated it can shut the Strait of Hormuz whenever it feels threatened — a card it didn't have before the conflict, and one Smith says it will hold "forever".

Even if oil does start flowing again, Smith says the economic recovery will likely take months. With the midterms about five months away, that recovery might not happen in time to help Republicans.

title.en: German broadcaster removes TV intro after Elon Musk takes legal action
title.zh: 德国广播公司在埃隆·马斯克采取法律行动后删除电视片头

summary.en: A German broadcaster removed a TV intro after tech billionaire Elon Musk initiated legal action, accusing the network of spreading "outrageous lies." The broadcaster, ZDF TV, responded to a "cease and desist" letter regarding the content.
summary.zh: 在科技亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克提起法律诉讼，指控德国一家广播公司散布“离谱的谎言”后，该广播公司删除了其电视节目片头。德国电视二台（ZDF TV）回应了一封“停止并终止”函。

body.en:
German public broadcaster ZDF has removed part of a report that claimed tech trillionaire Elon Musk had called for migrants to be hunted in Northern Ireland.

ZDF conceded its wording was "misleading" while Musk said "legal action is being taken against ZDF for their outrageous lies".

Violence erupted in Belfast last week, following a brutal knife attack in a street in the north of the city.

Police arrested a Sudanese man at the scene in north Belfast and he was later remanded in custody by a court on a charge of attempted murder.

The victim was seriously wounded and the court heard he had lost his left eye in last week's attack, which prompted unrest in Belfast and led to homes and vehicles being set alight.

The recent disorder in Northern Ireland attracted widespread international attention, including in Germany, where migration has also been a highly charged issue.

On Friday 12 June, a presenter introduced an edition of news magazine programme ZDFheute Live about the violence in Belfast entitled "How Musk is fuelling the protests" .

"A brutal attempted murder on a public street in Belfast," she explained in the now-removed introduction to the report. "Someone takes a video which goes viral. Following that, a racist mob is hunting migrants. The call for that came from a British right-wing extremist and tech billionaire Elon Musk."

Tommy Robinson, a well-known British far-right activist, had shared protest plans on Musk's social media platform X on 9 June, claiming that "the whole of the United Kingdom is hitting the streets tonight at 7pm following yet another invader attack on our people". However, he has suggested it is a lie to say that he has called for riots.

Musk quoted the post , saying "Only by protesting REPEATEDLY and LOUDLY will there be any change!!"

Musk said he would take legal action in response to the post highlighting ZDF's broadcast by German journalist Julian Reichelt, who runs NiUS, a relatively recent venture that has drawn comparisons with GB News in the UK or America's Fox News.

In a statement on Tuesday, ZDF told the BBC that Elon Musk had demanded a "cease and desist" declaration, through a German law firm.

"ZDF issued the declaration and removed the passage in question from the introduction," a spokesperson for the broadcaster said. "ZDF had already added a corrective transparency notice to the broadcast on Saturday."

Before removing the introduction altogether, ZDF had issued a clarification, saying that the wording had been "imprecise and therefore misleading".

The ZDF statement added: "Tommy Robinson called for protests after the knife attack in Belfast. The post was shared by Elon Musk."

body.zh: 德国公共广播公司 ZDF 删除了一篇报道的部分内容，该报道声称科技亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克呼吁在北爱尔兰追捕移民。 德国电视二台承认其措辞“具有误导性”，而马斯克则表示“正在对德国电视二台的无耻谎言采取法律行动”。 贝尔法斯特上周在该市北部的一条街道上发生了残酷的持刀袭击事件，随后爆发了暴力事件。 警方在贝尔法斯特北部的现场逮捕了一名苏丹男子，随后他因谋杀未遂罪被法庭还押。 受害者受重伤，法庭听说他在上周的袭击中失去了左眼，这引发了贝尔法斯特的骚乱，并导致房屋和车辆被纵火。 最近北爱尔兰的骚乱引起了国际社会的广泛关注，其中包括在德国，移民也是一个高度关注的问题。 6 月 12 日星期五，一位主持人介绍了有关贝尔法斯特暴力事件的新闻杂志节目《ZDFheute Live》的一期，题为“马斯克如何助长抗议活动”。 “贝尔法斯特的一条公共街道上发生了一起残酷的谋杀未遂事件，”她在现已删除的报告简介中解释道。 “有人拍摄了一段视频，并在网上疯传。随后，种族主义暴徒正在追捕移民。这一呼吁来自英国右翼极端分子、科技亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克。” 英国著名极右翼活动家罗宾逊于6月9日在马斯克的社交媒体平台X上分享了抗议计划，声称“今晚7点，在又一次入侵者袭击我们的人民后，整个英国都将走上街头”。然而，他表示，他呼吁骚乱的说法是谎言。 马斯克援引该帖子称，“只有反复大声抗议，才会有任何改变！” 马斯克表示，他将采取法律行动，以回应德国记者 Julian Reichelt 强调德国电视二台广播的帖子，后者经营着 NiUS，这是一家相对较新的企业，与英国的 GB News 或美国的福克斯新闻 (Fox News) 相比较。 德国电视二台在周二的一份声明中告诉英国广播公司，埃隆·马斯克已通过一家德国律师事务所要求“停止”声明。 “德国电视二台发表了声明，并从简介中删除了相关段落，”该广播公司的发言人表示。 “德国电视二台已在周六的广播中添加了纠正透明度通知。” 在完全删除介绍之前，德国电视二台发表了澄清声明，称该措辞“不准确，因此具有误导性”。 德国电视二台的声明补充道：“汤米·罗宾逊在贝尔法斯特发生持刀袭击事件后呼吁抗议。埃隆·马斯克分享了该帖子。” 这位科技大亨还拥有特斯拉和 SpaceX，并在 X 上拥有超过 2.4 亿粉丝，此前曾面临……

reflection.en: In public disputes, especially when accusations of falsehood are made, it is wise to remember that the first account often seems right until further examination. This incident reminds us of the importance of careful discernment and the need to hear all sides before forming a complete picture, fostering a more thoughtful public discourse.
reflection.zh: 在公共争议中，尤其当出现虚假指控时，我们应记住先发制人的说法往往看似有理，直到有另一方前来审察。这起事件提醒我们，在形成完整看法之前，仔细辨别和倾听各方声音至关重要，这有助于促进更深思熟虑的公共对话。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: Russian artist and Putin critic shot dead in Poland
title.zh: 俄罗斯艺术家、普京批评者在波兰遭枪杀

summary.en: Robert Kuzovkov, a Russian artist known for his caricatures of politicians including Vladimir Putin, has been shot dead in Poland. He used the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯艺术家罗伯特·库佐夫科夫在波兰被枪杀，他以笔名谢苗·斯克雷佩茨基创作包括弗拉基米尔·普京在内的政治人物漫画而闻名。

body.en:
Police in Poland are investigating the murder of a Russian artist and vocal critic of President Vladimir Putin.

Polish prosecutors said Robert K, known as the artist Semyon Skrepetsky, was shot dead on Monday morning in the Polish town of Biała Podlaska, about 40km (25 miles) from the Belarusian border.

The 44-year-old was shot five times in the head, chest and back in a car park in the town, located about 600m (2,000ft) from the Belarusian consulate.

Semyon Skrepetsky was the pseudonym used by Robert Kuzovkov. He was known for his caricatures of politicians, including Putin, Belarusian leader Alexander Lukashenko and Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov.

Police have detained two Belarusian citizens, aged 33 and 37, near the Belarusian consulate in the town and their role in the incident is still being determined, says Marcin Kozak, spokesman for the district prosecutor's office in the eastern city of Lublin.

Skrepetsky was given asylum in Biała Podlaska, a small town with a population of less than 60,000, after he left Russia in 2021 fearing criminal prosecution.

Kozak said the artist was approached by an unidentified gunman who fired two shots at him.

"When the victim fell to the ground, the perpetrator approached, fired three more shots and then quickly fled the scene. Robert K died at the scene," he added.

Five shell casings and one Geco 9mm Luger bullet were recovered from the crime scene, Kozak said.

Belarusian artist Vladislav Bokhan, who knew Skrepetsky, said he had found out about the shooting from Polish radio and immediately felt concerned: "I thought, that's where Skrepetsky lives. I know it's a very small town."

"The victim engaged in public artistic activities and used among other things, the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, under which he expressed criticism of the current policies of the Russian Federation authorities," Kozak said.

Skrepetsky's satirical cartoons had depicted Putin in the arms of Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin, Lukashenko as Adolf Hitler with a bucket of potatoes and Kadyrov and his son Adam with pigs' snouts.

He had also mocked Russian opposition figure Alexei Navalny as well as ordinary Ukrainians and his Polish address was freely available online. His work was posted on Telegram and on his YouTube channel.

Video posted on social media the night before his death showed the artist attending a Russia Day protest outside the Russian embassy in Berlin on Friday.

He had been carrying a painting caricaturing Putin and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin, as well as a Russian flag tied to his trousers that had been dragging along the road.

body.zh: 波兰警方正在调查一名俄罗斯艺术家和弗拉基米尔·普京总统的直言不讳的批评者被处决的谋杀案。 波兰检察官表示，艺术家谢苗·斯克雷佩茨基 (Semyon Skrepetsky) 的罗伯特·K (Robert K) 于周一早上在距离白俄罗斯边境约 40 公里（25 英里）的波兰城市比亚瓦波德拉斯卡 (Biała Podlaska) 被枪杀。 这名 44 岁的男子在距白俄罗斯领事馆约 600m 的市内一个停车场内头部、胸部和背部中了五枪。 谢苗·斯克雷佩茨基（Semyon Skrepetsky）是罗伯特·库佐夫科夫（Robert Kuzovkov）使用的笔名。他以对普京、白俄罗斯领导人亚历山大·卢卡申科和车臣领导人拉姆赞·卡德罗夫等政客的漫画而闻名。 卢布林地区检察官办公室发言人马尔辛·科扎克(Marcin Kozak)表示，一名身份不明的枪手接近这位艺术家，并向他开了两枪。 “当受害者倒地时，肇事者靠近，又开了三枪，然后迅速逃离现场。罗伯特·K当场死亡，”他补充道。 科扎克说，犯罪现场发现了五枚弹壳和一颗 Geco 9 毫米鲁格子弹。 警方在白俄罗斯驻该市领事馆附近拘留了两名分别为 33 岁和 37 岁的白俄罗斯公民。科扎克说，他们在这起事件中的角色仍在确定中。 科扎克说：“受害者从事公共艺术活动，并使用笔名谢苗·斯克雷佩茨基（Semyon Skrepetsky），他用这个笔名表达了对俄罗斯联邦当局现行政策的批评。” 最近在社交媒体上发布的视频显示，6 月 12 日，斯克雷佩茨基在俄罗斯驻柏林大使馆外参加了俄罗斯日抗议活动。 他随身带着一幅描绘普京和苏联领导人约瑟夫·斯大林的画作，他的裤子上还系着一面俄罗斯国旗，一直拖在路上。

reflection.en: The tragic death of an artist known for his political critiques highlights the profound risks faced by those who speak truth to power. Matthew 5:10 reminds us that there is a spiritual blessing for those who suffer persecution for righteousness' sake, even when the cost is immense. It calls us to reflect on the courage required to stand for truth in a world...
reflection.zh: 一位以政治讽刺漫画闻名的艺术家不幸遇害，这凸显了那些敢于向权力说真话的人所面临的巨大风险。马太福音5:10提醒我们，为义受逼迫的人是有福的，即使为此付出巨大的代价。这促使我们反思，在一个常常试图压制真理的世界中，坚持真理所需的勇气。

verse.textEn: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
verse.textZh: 为义受逼迫的人有福了，因为天国是他们的。

title.en: Why women's inheritance reform has stalled across Arab world
title.zh: 阿拉伯世界女性继承权改革为何停滞不前

summary.en: Sharia-based inheritance laws continue to disadvantage millions of women across the Middle East, leading to calls for reform that has largely stalled.
summary.zh: 中东地区基于伊斯兰教法的继承法持续使数百万女性处于不利地位，尽管有改革呼声，但相关改革进展缓慢。

body.en:
Sharia-based inheritance laws continue to disadvantage millions of women across the Middle East. What could prompt real change for the next generation of girls?

The death of her husband pushed 60-year-old Moroccan widow Meryem into a deep crisis.  Speaking with  Moroccan magazine Egalite Mag in February, she said it wasn't just the sadness over her loss that has made her feel vulnerable.

"I find myself alone, facing his family, treated like an enemy even though I built this life with him for 30 years," she said, asking that her last name not be published for fear of retaliation from her late husband's family.

Meryem's husband had made a point of providing for her future by purchasing an apartment in her name. But  shortly after his death, his relatives claimed in court that the property belonged to them, according to one of the Sharia-based inheritance rules, taasib. Under taasib, in cases where a deceased man leaves daughters but no sons, male relatives inherit substantial portions of the estate alongside the daughters and widow.

Eventually, a Moroccan court ruled in Meryem's favor. Her husband had legally and indisputably transferred the apartment to her during his lifetime, which is permitted under Islamic inheritance law.

"It's the only thing I have left, and I rent it out for a modest income," said Meryem, adding that all other assets — a car, bank accounts — remain tied up in inheritance disputes.

"We regularly see cases where the husband dies and the wife has to move out of the couple's marital home because the property must be divided among the heirs," said Dörthe Engelcke of the Max Planck Institute for Foreign and International Private Law in Hamburg.

"If widows were allowed to continue living in their marital homes, it would be an incredibly significant change," she told DW, adding that "it would contribute greatly to the social stability of the surviving wives."

While governments across the Middle East and North Africa have expanded women's rights in areas such as domestic  violence protection , family law and legal autonomy, inheritance reform remains one of the region's most sensitive issues, according to rights advocates and legal scholars.

"In general, sons continue to receive twice the inheritance share of daughters because — so the reasoning goes — unlike daughters, sons are expected to provide financially for their families," said Elham Manea, an adjunct professor at the University of Zurich and author of the 2011 book "The Arab State and Women's Rights: The Trap of Authoritarian Governance."

body.zh: 基于伊斯兰教法的继承法继续使中东数百万妇女处于不利地位。什么可以促使下一代女孩发生真正的改变？ 丈夫的去世让 60 岁的摩洛哥寡妇梅耶姆陷入了深深的危机。 二月，她在接受摩洛哥杂志 Egalite Mag 采访时表示，让她感到脆弱的不仅仅是失去亲人的悲伤。 “我发现自己孤身一人，面对着他的家人，尽管我和他一起生活了30年，但我还是被当作敌人对待，”她说，并要求不要公开她的姓氏，因为担心遭到已故丈夫家人的报复。 梅耶姆的丈夫为了她的未来，以她的名义购买了一套公寓。但在他去世后不久，他的亲戚在法庭上声称，根据基于伊斯兰教法的继承规则之一“塔西卜”，该财产属于他们。根据塔西卜制度，如果死者留下女儿但没有留下儿子，男性亲属将与女儿和寡妇一起继承大部分遗产。 最终，摩洛哥法院做出了对梅耶姆有利的裁决。她的丈夫在生前合法且无可争议地将公寓转让给了她，这是伊斯兰继承法所允许的。 梅耶姆说：“这是我唯一剩下的东西，我把它出租以获得微薄的收入。”他补充说，所有其他资产——汽车、银行账户——仍然与继承纠纷有关。 汉堡马克斯·普朗克外国和国际私法研究所的德特·恩格尔克说：“我们经常看到丈夫去世，妻子不得不搬出夫妻双方的婚姻住所的情况，因为财产必须在继承人之间分配。” 她告诉德国之声：“如果允许寡妇继续住在她们的婚姻家里，这将是一个令人难以置信的重大变化。”她补充道，“这将极大地促进幸存妻子的社会稳定。” 权利倡导者和法律学者表示，虽然中东和北非各国政府在家庭暴力保护、家庭法和法律自治等领域扩大了妇女权利，但继承改革仍然是该地区最敏感的问题之一。 苏黎世大学兼职教授、2011 年出版的《阿拉伯国家与妇女权利：威权治理的陷阱》一书的作者埃勒姆·马内亚 (Elham Manea) 表示：“一般来说，儿子继承的遗产份额是女儿的两倍，原因是——与女儿不同，儿子应该为家庭提供经济来源。” “然而，在实践中，这种假设越来越不能反映社会现实，”她告诉德国之声，并补充说“许多女性被剥夺了……

reflection.en: The stalled reform of inheritance laws highlights the ongoing struggle for justice for many women. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us to speak up for those whose rights are denied, advocating for fairness and equity for all who are vulnerable. This call to uphold the rights of the disadvantaged remains vital in seeking a more just future.

title.en: Failed joint jet project highlights Europe's defense dilemma
title.zh: 失败的联合喷气式飞机项目凸显欧洲防务困境

summary.en: A Franco-German fighter jet project has collapsed, and a joint battle tank program is faltering, illustrating how national industrial interests can take precedence over shared defense objectives in Europe.
summary.zh: 法德联合战斗机项目已告失败，而一项联合主战坦克项目也步履维艰，这表明在欧洲，国家工业利益有时会超越共同的防务目标。

body.en:
The collapse of a Franco-German fighter jet project and a faltering joint battle tank program show how national industrial interests can outweigh common defense objectives.

Anyone who wants to be taken seriously in the European defense industry shows up to Eurosatory, France's largest defense trade show, held every two years. This week, the industry is once again showcasing its latest advances at the sprawling exhibition grounds in Villepinte, near Paris. More than 2,000 exhibitors mingle with military officials, politicians, and industry professionals.

With  order books full , the mood should be upbeat. European governments want to reduce their defense dependency on the United States and are investing hundreds of billions of euros to advance that goal.

However, the prevailing optimism is being tempered by disappointment.  Europe's most ambitious defense project aimed at greater strategic autonomy effectively collapsed just days ago: Germany and France dealt what appears to be a fatal blow to their joint sixth-generation fighter aircraft program. The centerpiece of the Future Combat Air System (FCAS) will not be built as a joint project after all.

French Defense Minister Catherine Vautrin avoided the subject in her opening speech on Monday. Nevertheless, there are growing signs that Paris and Berlin have become deadlocked not only over the fighter jet program, but also their joint battle tank project.

President Emmanuel Macron and former Chancellor Angela Merkel launched FCAS in 2017 in response to Brexit and the election of US President Donald Trump to the White House. The fighter aircraft initiative was accompanied by a Franco-German tank program called the Main Ground Combat System (MGCS). Under the arrangement, France was to take the lead on the fighter jet project, while Germany would oversee the tank program.

Since then, President Macron has repeatedly warned that if FCAS fails, MGCS could ultimately suffer the same fate.

Last weekend, Armin Papperger, head of Germany's largest defense company Rheinmetall, fueled the uncertainty. Papperger told Welt am Sonntag that Paris is considering drastically cutting funding for the project, but said that no final decision has been made.

"I take these warnings very seriously," said Ulrike Franke of the European Council of Foreign Relations (ECFR) in Paris, speaking to the German broadcaster Deutschlandfunk . She added that the tank project has faced increasing difficulties and progressed more slowly than FCAS from the outset.

Meanwhile, Germany's Defense Ministry said that  Germany and France had agreed to continue developing MGCS in a "platform-independent" manner and to focus on the program's core elements. Whether that...
body.zh: 法德战斗机项目的失败和摇摇欲坠的联合作战坦克计划表明，国家工业利益如何能够超越共同的国防目标。 任何想要在欧洲国防工业中受到认真对待的人都会参加每两年举办一次的法国最大的国防贸易展 Eurosatory。本周，该行业再次在巴黎附近维勒班特广阔的展览场地展示其最新进展。超过 2,000 家参展商与军方官员、政治家和行业专业人士交往。 订单已满，心情应该会很乐观。欧洲各国政府希望减少对美国的国防依赖，并正在投资数千亿欧元来推进这一目标。 然而，普遍的乐观情绪正在因失望而减弱。 欧洲最雄心勃勃的旨在实现更大战略自主权的国防项目在几天前实际上宣告失败：德国和法国对其联合第六代战斗机计划造成了致命的打击。 毕竟，未来作战空中系统（FCAS）的核心部分不会作为一个联合项目建造。 法国国防部长凯瑟琳·沃特琳在周一的开幕致辞中回避了这个话题。然而，越来越多的迹象表明，巴黎和柏林不仅在战斗机项目上陷入僵局，而且在联合作战坦克项目上也陷入僵局。 总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙 (Emmanuel Macron) 和前总理安格拉·默克尔 (Angela Merkel) 于 2017 年推出 FCAS，以应对英国脱欧和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普入主白宫。 战斗机计划伴随着法德坦克计划，称为主地面作战系统（MGCS）。根据安排，法国将牵头战斗机项目，而德国将监督坦克项目。 此后，马克龙总统多次警告称，如果FCAS失败，MGCS最终可能会遭受同样的命运。 上周末，德国最大的国防公司莱茵金属公司的负责人阿明·帕珀格(Armin Papperger)加剧了这种不确定性。 帕珀格告诉《周日世界报》，巴黎正在考虑大幅削减该项目的资金，但表示尚未做出最终决定。 “我非常认真地对待这些警告，”巴黎欧洲对外关系委员会 (ECFR) 的乌尔里克·弗兰克 (Ulrike Franke) 在接受德国广播公司 Deutschlandfunk 采访时表示。她补充说，坦克项目从一开始就面临着越来越多的困难，而且进展速度比 FCAS 慢。 与此同时，德国国防部表示，德国和法国已同意继续以“平台独立”的方式开发 MGCS，并重点关注该计划的核心要素。无论是...

reflection.en: The collapse of joint defense projects highlights the challenge of prioritizing collective good over individual interests. Philippians 2:3 reminds us that true progress often requires setting aside selfish ambition and valuing shared objectives. When nations or groups prioritize their own gain above common goals, even vital projects can falter.
reflection.zh: 联合防务项目的失败凸显了将集体利益置于个体利益之上的挑战。腓立比书2:3提醒我们，真正的进步往往需要放下自私的野心，重视共同的目标。当国家或团体将自身利益置于共同目标之上时，即使是至关重要的项目也可能停滞不前。

title.en: Pakistan raises defense spending amid regional conflicts
title.zh: 巴基斯坦在地区冲突中增加国防开支

summary.en: The sharp hike in defense spending highlights lessons Pakistan has learned from recent conflicts with India and a growing focus on new warfare technologies, regardless of economic constraints imposed by the IMF.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The sharp hike in defense spending highlights lessons Pakistan has learned from recent conflicts with India and a growing focus on new warfare technologies, regardless of economic constraints imposed by the IMF.

The Pakistani government last week presented a draft budget to lawmakers that hikes defense spending by 18% to 3 trillion rupees ($10.8 billion/€9.3 billion).

Pakistan's finance minister, Muhammad Aurangzeb, said the increase was intended to make the country "invincible due to the uncertainty in the region." Analysts say key considerations are evolving military technologies and emerging threats.

"Future conflicts will no longer be confined to two adversaries," said Islamabad-based defense analyst Maria Sultan. "They will be shaped by weapons and technology flowing from multiple countries, fought across land, air, cyber and electronic domains simultaneously."

Sultan told DW that wars in Ukraine  and the Middle East as well as last year's India-Pakistan conflict — which brought the nuclear-armed neighbors to the brink of all-out war — have reshaped how military planners think.

In May 2025, New Delhi launched Operation Sindoor in retaliation for a deadly mass shooting at  Pahalgam , a popular resort town in India-administered Kashmir, in which at least 26 mostly Indian Hindu tourists were killed.

India said the Pakistan-based group Lashkar-e-Taiba, considered a terrorist organization by the UN, had carried out the attack. New Delhi also accused Islamabad of backing the group, with the Pakistani government denying the allegation.

India and Pakistan both claim Kashmir in its entirety, but each country only controls a section of territory, making the Muslim-majority region a flash point in the larger India-Pakistan geopolitical rivalry.

The clashes following the Pahalgam attack raised concerns about strategic stability in South Asia and sparked debate about the limits of nuclear deterrence between rival nuclear powers.

"The conflict demonstrated that atomic weapons do not necessarily prevent conventional conflict below the nuclear threshold," said Qamar Cheema, executive director of the Sanober Institute, an Islamabad-based think tank.

Pakistan's military planners are grappling with a security environment shaped by India's continuing military modernization and the growing role of drones , cyber capabilities and precision-guided weapons in modern warfare, according to Cheema. 

Islamabad is also embroiled in a conflict with neighboring Afghanistan , particularly in its western provinces of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

In February, Islamabad declared it was in "open war" with Kabul, following a rise in militant attacks on civilians and security forces inside Pakistan.

title.en: Is the Iran war weakening the US' superpower status?
title.zh: 伊朗战争是否正在削弱美国的超级大国地位？

summary.en: The US is still unrivaled in its ability to project military strength around the world, but Iran's success in blocking the Strait of Hormuz has raised tough question on America's role as protector of global trade.
summary.zh: 尽管美国在全球军事力量投射方面仍无与伦比，但伊朗成功封锁霍尔木兹海峡的事件，引发了人们对美国作为全球贸易保护者角色的严峻质疑。

body.en:
The US is still unrivaled in its ability to project military strength around the world, but Iran's success in blocking the Strait of Hormuz has raised tough question on America's role as protector of global trade.

"Ships of the World, start your engines," US President Donald Trump said while announcing a deal with Iran to end the conflict he launched along with Israel more than three months ago.

The online post on Sunday also saw Trump "fully authorize" the toll-free reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

The US and Iran are due to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in Geneva later this week. With the details still under wraps , Trump later said Hormuz would "fully reopen" only after the deal is signed.

But unconfirmed reports on the MoU published in pro-regime Iranian media claim that Tehran's future role in Hormuz is still up for negotiation. The Fars news agency reported that "Iranian-Omani sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz" had been added to negotiations at the last minute, while claiming that the US had "accepted" that fees would be paid to Iran.

When asked for clarification on Monday, US Vice President JD Vance told the CNBC news outlet that Washington's "expectation is that the strait is going to be opened in a toll-free way for the long term," adding, "that's the sort of thing that we're going to figure out in these technical negotiations."

Opacity aside, it is clear that the US is not able to dictate the terms regarding the Strait of Hormuz to Iran, despite Washington's overwhelming military strength.

Moreover, Iran's ability to use drones, mines and small boats to shut down free movement of shipping has shed uncomfortable light on the role of US power in protecting freedom of navigation and ensuring free trade.

"The Iran war showed America's exceptional military prowess — and its inability to convert those capabilities into anything resembling strategic victory," said Rebecca Lissner, senior fellow for US foreign policy and director of the Future of American Strategy Initiative at the US Council on Foreign Relations (CFR).

"This is a blow to America's image as a global superpower and undercuts its status as a guarantor of freedom of navigation. This war has left the United States in a weaker position than when the war began," she told DW.

Trump laid out an array of objectives when launching the war, including the "annihilation" of Iran's conventional navy. This one objective, at least, seems to have been met — the Center for International and Strategic Studies (CSIS) has assessed that "Iran lost the majority of its naval capability in less than 10 days."

body.zh: 美国在世界各地投射军事力量的能力仍然无与伦比，但伊朗成功封锁霍尔木兹海峡，对美国作为全球贸易保护者的角色提出了严峻的质疑。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在宣布与伊朗达成协议以结束三个多月前与以色列发起的冲突时说道，“世界的船只，启动引擎”。 周日的网上帖子还显示，特朗普“完全授权”免费重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。 美国和伊朗定于本周晚些时候在日内瓦签署谅解备忘录（MoU）。由于细节仍处于保密状态，特朗普后来表示，只有在协议签署后，霍尔木兹才会“全面重新开放”。 但亲政权的伊朗媒体发表的有关谅解备忘录的未经证实的报道称，德黑兰未来在霍尔木兹的角色仍有待谈判。法尔斯通讯社报道称，“伊朗和阿曼对霍尔木兹海峡的主权”在最后一刻被纳入谈判，同时声称美国已“接受”向伊朗支付费用。 周一，当被要求澄清时，美国副总统 JD 万斯告诉 CNBC 新闻媒体，华盛顿“期望该海峡将以长期免费的方式开放”，并补充道，“这就是我们将在这些技术谈判中解决的问题。” 撇开不透明不谈，很明显，尽管华盛顿拥有压倒性的军事实力，但美国无法决定有关伊朗通往霍尔木兹海峡的条款。 此外，伊朗利用无人机、水雷和小船来阻止航运自由流动的能力，让人们对美国在保护航行自由和确保自由贸易方面所发挥的作用产生了不安的认识。 美国外交政策高级研究员兼美国外交关系委员会未来美国战略倡议主任丽贝卡·利斯纳表示：“伊朗战争展示了美国非凡的军事实力，但它却无力将这些能力转化为战略胜利。” “这对美国作为全球超级大国的形象造成了打击，并削弱了其作为航行自由保障者的地位。这场战争使美国处于比战争开始时更弱势的地位，”她告诉德国之声。 特朗普在发动战争时提出了一系列目标，包括“歼灭”伊朗常规海军。至少这一目标似乎已经实现——国际与战略研究中心 (CSIS) 评估称，“伊朗在不到 10 天内失去了大部分海军能力”。 但伊朗不需要常规海军来劫持霍尔木兹的船只。事实证明，其对海湾能源设施进行的基于无人机的不对称打击......

title.en: US military plans major war stockpile on Australian soil
title.zh: 美国军方计划在澳大利亚领土上储存大量战争物资

summary.en: The massive buildup of weapons is part of an Asia-wide regional defence strategy to counter the rise of China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US military is planning a permanent war-ready weapons stockpile for its marine corps on Australia's southeast coast beyond the range of most Chinese missiles, tender documents show and officials confirmed to the Agence France-Presse news agency (AFP).

The development of the stockpile, a first for the US marine corps in Australia, comes as the United States is keen to leverage the continent's strategic location in the South Pacific to counter China's rapid military build-up, analysts said.

The US marine corps began global prepositioning of military supplies during the Cold War — using floating stores on ships and caves in Norway where weapons, ammunition and vehicles to sustain thousands of troops are kept.

The first land stockpile in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to open this year in the Philippines, close to potential flashpoints in the South China Sea.

Documents published by the US navy this month show advanced planning for an even larger Australian stockpile, with US$30 million ($42.4M) allocated to build warehouses and offices in southeastern Victoria state for "critical forward provisioning".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The Australian stockpile, expected to reach full capacity by 2028, will be kept in Melbourne before being moved to US warehouses to be constructed next year at an Australian military base at Bandiana in rural Victoria, tender documents show.

Australia does not permit foreign military bases on its soil, a sensitive issue in a country that has a security alliance with the United States and is hosting an increasing variety of US forces on rotation at Australian defence bases.

The US navy is engaging a global defence contractor to employ around 110 engineers, mechanics, material and safety specialists to manage the Australian stockpile, which includes "crew-served weapons", the documents show.

"Marine corps activities in Australia support integrated global sustainment by maintaining ready-for-issue equipment and supplies for operations and exercises across the Indo-Pacific," a US marine corps forces pacific spokesperson told AFP.

The spokesperson declined to comment on contract details or force planning assumptions but said marines' equipment is kept at "high readiness".

Contracting arrangements and the operation of the facility would be made in close coordination with Australia's Department of Defence.

body.en:
The Iranian football team has been met by hundreds of anti-regime protesters in the most politically charged match of this year's FIFA World Cup so far.

The Group G opener against New Zealand, which ended in a 2-2 draw, at the Los Angeles Stadium on Tuesday morning (AEST), came just a day after the United States and Iran announced a peace deal to end the war in the Middle East.

Outside the stadium, many waved the Lion and Sun flag, Iran's national flag before the 1979 revolution, which is now associated with the Iranian opposition and banned in Iran. Others also waved Israeli and US flags.

One anti-regime protester heckled Iranian supporters waiting in line to enter the match, giving them the middle finger, grabbing an Iranian flag from a fan in line and stomping on it.

FIFA banned fans from bringing the pre-revolution flag into World Cup matches, citing its rules prohibiting flags or political apparel.

But numerous people carrying the lion-and-sun flag or wearing t-shirts with the symbol passed through security at the stadium without issue.

Iran had threatened to halt the match if unofficial flags were brought in or slogans were chanted, but the match proceeded as planned.

Assal Pahlevan, an organiser with Democracy for Iran, told SBS News she was protesting the flag ban.

"Any sport, it's volleyball or basketball or football, it doesn't matter which sport is it, you can say whatever you want to say."

Los Angeles is home to one of the largest Iranian diaspora communities in the world, many of whom are descendants of Iranians who fled after the revolution and oppose the Iranian government.

Inside the stadium, the Iranian national anthem was booed, but Iran also enjoyed support from many in the crowd who erupted into cheers when they equalised in the first half.

"I'm here to support Iran. We're going to win this game," said 57-year-old Mehdi Jafari, wearing an Iran football shirt, going into the stadium ahead of the match.

"We're very proud of our country. We're here to support Iran. I think we should all let go of the politics and just go in and cheer on the Team Melli."

After months of debate about whether they would participate in the tournament, the Iranian national football team arrived in Los Angeles on Sunday afternoon, local time, from Tijuana, Mexico, where they had relocated their base camp due to security concerns related to the conflict.

Hours after their arrival, US President Donald Trump announced an agreement to end hostilities between the two countries , which began when the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.

Two-thirds of people now live in countries that have slipped below the replacement rate – 2.1 births per woman – required for a stable population. The world’s two most populous nations, which pursued cruel and coercive policies to cut births, both face shrinking populations. summary.en: The massive buildup of weapons is part of an Asia-wide regional defence strategy to counter the rise of China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US military is planning a permanent war-ready weapons stockpile for its marine corps on Australia's southeast coast beyond the range of most Chinese missiles, tender documents show and officials confirmed to the Agence France-Presse news agency (AFP).

The development of the stockpile, a first for the US marine corps in Australia, comes as the United States is keen to leverage the continent's strategic location in the South Pacific to counter China's rapid military build-up, analysts said.

The US marine corps began global prepositioning of military supplies during the Cold War — using floating stores on ships and caves in Norway where weapons, ammunition and vehicles to sustain thousands of troops are kept.

The first land stockpile in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to open this year in the Philippines, close to potential flashpoints in the South China Sea.

Documents published by the US navy this month show advanced planning for an even larger Australian stockpile, with US$30 million ($42.4M) allocated to build warehouses and offices in southeastern Victoria state for "critical forward provisioning".

The Australian stockpile, expected to reach full capacity by 2028, will be kept in Melbourne before being moved to US warehouses to be constructed next year at an Australian military base at Bandiana in rural Victoria, tender documents show.

Australia does not permit foreign military bases on its soil, a sensitive issue in a country that has a security alliance with the United States and is hosting an increasing variety of US forces on rotation at Australian defence bases.

The US navy is engaging a global defence contractor to employ around 110 engineers, mechanics, material and safety specialists to manage the Australian stockpile, which includes "crew-served weapons", the documents show.

"Marine corps activities in Australia support integrated global sustainment by maintaining ready-for-issue equipment and supplies for operations and exercises across the Indo-Pacific," a US marine corps forces pacific spokesperson told AFP.

The spokesperson declined to comment on contract details or force planning assumptions but said marines' equipment is kept at "high readiness".

Contracting arrangements and the operation of the facility would be made in close coordination with Australia's Department of Defence.

"These activities improve responsiveness, strengthen interoperability with allies and partners, and support a range of missions across the Indo-Pacific," the spokesperson said, using an alternative description for the Asia-Pacific region.

body.zh: 电动汽车变得越来越便宜、越来越高效，而且行驶距离比以往任何时候都更远。中国正在推动这一转型，但欧洲和其他国家正在快速追赶。 全球电动汽车 (EV) 市场的增长速度远远快于预期。短短六年内，销量增长了十倍，到 2025 年，全球电动汽车销量将达到约 2100 万辆。 中国和欧洲处于领先地位，但世界其他地区的市场也在快速增长。 中国长期以来一直在投资太阳能和风能以及电池技术——电动汽车最关键的组成部分。 得益于先进的研究和大规模生产，电动汽车电池成本大幅下降。如今，它们的成本仅为 10 年前的四分之一，而且价格还在继续下降。 中国是世界上最大的汽车市场，消费者正在从政府的产业战略中获益。自 2024 年以来，电动汽车的成本低于内燃机汽车，国家多年来一直在迅速扩大充电基础设施，而且中国的电力非常实惠。 2015年，电动汽车仅占中国新车销量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，这一比例已攀升至 61%。 电动汽车依靠电力运行并通过电缆充电。在全球范围内，三分之二的电动汽车是所谓的电池电动汽车 (BEV)，仅由电力驱动。剩下的三分之一还配备了燃气发动机，用于长途旅行时的备用——这些被称为增程电动汽车 (EREV) 或插电式混合动力电动汽车 (PHEV)。 相比之下，所谓的混合动力电动汽车 (HEV) 始终需要汽油或柴油来为其内燃机提供动力。电动机提供一些帮助，仅通过再生制动产生电力。这项技术在一定程度上降低了城市驾驶的燃油消耗，但混合动力汽车在国际统计中并未被算作电动汽车。 2018年，电动汽车仅占欧盟新车注册量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，售出的新车中近三分之一是电动汽车。 北欧处于领先地位。在挪威，现在销售的几乎所有新车都是电动汽车（99%），其次是丹麦（82%）和瑞典（65%）。该地区各国政府支持气候友好型出行，并正在扩大充电基础设施。 在英国，2026 年 4 月注册的新车中有 39% 是电动汽车，其次是德国（37%）和法国（32%）。在这三个国家，电动汽车销量与去年同月相比都翻了一番。 近年来，美国市场陷入停滞。 2023 年至 2025 年间，电动汽车占...

reflection.en: The rapid advancements in electric vehicle technology, making them cheaper and more efficient, reflect a remarkable acceleration of human knowledge and innovation. This progress reminds us of the human capacity to explore and develop new solutions, continually expanding our understanding and capabilities.

title.en: Girlfriends review – love and growing pains in queer coming-of-age tale that goes from Hong Kong to Taiwan
title.zh: 女朋友》影评：一部从香港到台湾的酷儿成长故事，充满爱与成长的烦恼

summary.en: The film "Girlfriends" is a romantic drama by Tracy Choi, following one woman's journey from high school to her mid-30s, exploring love and the challenges of growing up within a queer coming-of-age narrative set between Hong Kong and Taiwan.
summary.zh: 电影《女朋友》是崔允信执导的一部浪漫剧情片，讲述了一名女性从高中到三十多岁的人生旅程，探讨了在香港和台湾之间发生的酷儿成长故事中的爱与成长烦恼。

body.en: A trio of actors play one woman from high school to her mid-30s in Tracy Choi’s thoughtful romantic drama It can stretch credibility a little when an actor plays the same character over a long time span in one film. Richard Linklater solved the problem in Boyhood by shooting scenes over succeeding years; AI and de-ageing effects are now an option. With this intimate queer coming-of-age drama, film-maker Tracy Choi instead casts a trio of actors to play one woman from high school to her mid-30s. The three don’t look particularly alike; their temperaments overlap but are by no means identical. The point is perhaps to show how intense the transitions into adulthood are, how unrecognisable are the people we used to be. Working backwards, Girlfriends begins in Hong Kong, where 34-year-old film director Lok (Fish Liew) lives with her actor girlfriend Bei (Jennifer Yu). Five years earlier, Choi released a feature film, but her career has stalled. She is directionless and restless. Bei is also applying pressure to buy a flat and have a baby. The film then rewinds 12 years, to Taiwan, when Lok was a student with spiky orange hair, known as Choi (played by Elizabeth Tang). Some of the best scenes in the film come when her parents visit from Macau; Choi and her girlfriend Qing (Han Ning) have been pretending to be flatmates. Then, as the four of them eat dinner one night, unwilling to keep up the charade, Choi grabs Qing’s hand fiercely over the dinner table. She is coming out to her parents; they understand but say nothing. Another film might give us a big showdown, but this is probably how it would have happened in real life. Continue reading...
body.zh: 在 Tracy Choi 这部深思熟虑的浪漫剧中，三位演员扮演一名从高中到 30 多岁的女性。当一个演员在一部电影中长时间扮演同一个角色时，可信度会有所提高。理查德·林克莱特在《少年时代》中通过连续几年拍摄场景解决了这个问题。人工智能和抗衰老效果现在是一种选择。在这部亲密的酷儿成长剧中，电影制片人崔西·崔 (Tracy Choi) 聘请了三名演员来扮演一名从高中到 30 多岁的女性。这三个人看起来并不是特别相似。他们的性格有重叠，但绝不相同。重点也许是为了表明向成年的转变是多么激烈，我们过去的样子是多么难以辨认。时光倒流，《女朋友》的故事发生在香港，34 岁的电影导演乐（刘静茹饰）和她的演员女友贝（余珍妮饰）住在一起。五年前，崔发布了一部故事片，但她的事业却陷入了停滞。她没有方向，焦躁不安。贝还施加压力，要求买一套公寓并生孩子。影片随后将时间倒回12年前的台湾，当时乐还是一名留着尖尖橙色头发的学生，名叫崔（伊丽莎白·唐饰）。影片中一些最精彩的场景出现在她的父母从澳门来访时；崔和女友青（韩宁饰）一直假装是室友。然后，有一天晚上，当他们四个人吃晚饭时，崔不愿继续玩这个游戏，在餐桌上猛烈地抓住了庆的手。她向父母出柜了；他们明白但什么也没说。另一部电影可能会给我们带来一场大对决，但这可能就是现实生活中发生的情况。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This film explores the complex journey of self-discovery and relationships, highlighting the universal human experience of love and growing pains. In every person's unique path of identity and connection, we are reminded of the profound truth that each individual is created in the image of God, possessing inherent dignity and worth.
reflection.zh: 这部电影探讨了自我发现和关系的复杂旅程，突显了爱与成长烦恼的普世人性体验。在每个人独特的身份和联结之路上，我们都被提醒着一个深刻的真理：每个人都是按照雅伟的形象被创造的，拥有固有的尊严和价值。

body.en: Import and export figures come as European leaders prepare to meet this week to address growing imbalance The EU’s trade deficit with China has reached a record €1bn (£0.8bn) a day, according to official trade data, fuelling concerns over the future of Europe’s “industrial backbone”. The gap between the EU’s imports from China and exports to China amounted to €31.9bn in April, according to the latest import and export data from the EU statistics body Eurostat. Continue reading...

This calls for wisdom and integrity in seeking fair and sustainable economic relationships for all.
reflection.zh: 每日十亿欧元的贸易逆差凸显了主要贸易伙伴之间巨大的经济失衡。箴言提醒我们，尽管人类系统可能容忍这种差异，但公义和公平的平衡才是真正令雅伟喜悦的。这呼吁我们在寻求对各方都公平和可持续的经济关系时，需要智慧和正直。

body.en: The 70-year-old has been prosecuted for his artworks under a law that did not exist when they were created. He should be freed Sixty years ago, Mao Zedong launched the Cultural Revolution – a decade of fanaticism that consumed China. Perhaps 2 million people, from top leaders to impoverished farmers, were killed or driven to suicide for political “crimes” or their family background. Tens of millions more, including the father of China’s leader, Xi Jinping, were hounded. The party, and most of those who lived through the movement, prefer to forget it. But the years of chaos, violence, zealotry and stagnation, which ended only with Mao’s death, have left deep scars. Among the many victims was a factory worker whose young sons grew up to become celebrated artists. Their work addressed the devastation wrought by the era, including through satirical images of Mao . body.zh: 这位 70 岁的老人因其艺术作品而受到起诉，而这项法律在创作这些艺术作品时并不存在。他应该被释放 六十年前，毛泽东发动了文化大革命——十年的狂热席卷了中国。大约有 200 万人，从最高领导人到贫困农民，因政治“犯罪”或家庭背景而被杀害或被迫自杀。还有数千万人遭到追捕，其中包括中国领导人习近平的父亲。该党以及大多数经历过这场运动的人宁愿忘记它。但那些混乱、暴力、狂热和停滞的岁月，直到毛泽东去世才结束，留下了深深的伤痕。在众多受害者中，有一名工厂工人，他的年幼的儿子长大后成为了著名的艺术家。他们的作品通过讽刺毛泽东的形象来讲述那个时代造成的破坏。继续阅读...

summary.en: British pop star Jessie J made a triumphant return to the lucrative Chinese music market, a week after announcing she was cancer-free. Her success in the country's music scene has inspired other Western acts to seek similar opportunities since her breakout in 2018.
summary.zh: 英国流行歌星Jessie J在宣布自己“癌症痊愈”一周后，凯旋回归利润丰厚的中国音乐市场。自2018年她在中国取得突破性成功以来，她的经历也激励了其他西方艺人寻求类似的机会。

body.en: Other western acts have attempted to crack country’s music scene since singer’s breakout success in 2018 One week after announcing she was “cancer free”, the British pop star Jessie J did what any recovering patient would do and travelled thousands of miles around the world to perform for an audience of more than a billion people. On 29 May, the singer-songwriter, whose real name is Jessica Cornish, belted out a stage-rattling rendition of Frank Sinatra’s My Way on the stage of Singer, a hugely popular Chinese singing competition similar to The Voice. She also performed her new song, California, briefly adapting the lyrics to change California to Changsha, the Chinese city where Singer is hosted. Continue reading...
body.zh: 自 2018 年歌手取得突破性成功以来，其他西方艺人也试图闯入乡村音乐界。在宣布自己“癌症痊愈”一周后，英国流行歌星杰西·J (Jessie J) 做了任何康复患者都会做的事情，长途跋涉到世界各地为超过 10 亿观众表演。 5 月 29 日，这位真名杰西卡·康尼什 (Jessica Cornish) 的创作型歌手在《歌手》舞台上高声演唱了弗兰克·辛纳屈 (Frank Sinatra) 的《我的路》(My Way)。《歌手》是一项与《好声音》类似的非常受欢迎的中国歌唱比赛。她还演唱了她的新歌《加州》，简单地修改了歌词，将加州改为《歌手》所在的中国城市长沙。继续阅读...

reflection.en: After facing a serious illness, Jessie J's return to the stage embodies a powerful message of renewed strength and purpose. Her journey reminds us that even after periods of great weakness, there is hope for soaring again, finding fresh vigor for the path ahead.
reflection.zh: 面对重疾之后，Jessie J重返舞台，这体现了力量和目标重获新生的有力信息。她的旅程提醒我们，即使在极度虚弱之后，仍有希望再次翱翔，为前方的道路找到新的活力。

title.en: Many Aussies want to buy at the bottom. But how far can property prices fall?
title.zh: 许多澳大利亚人想在市场底部买入。但房价能跌多深？

summary.en: Property prices may be softening, but experts warn trying to pick the bottom of the market is rarely simple.
summary.zh: 房地产价格可能正在走软，但专家警告说，试图在市场底部买入通常并非易事。

body.en:
For more than two years, Mary Latham has spent weekends walking through open homes across Sydney’s inner west.

The 37-year-old has inspected properties in the Canada Bay area most weeks for the past two years, and was initially held back from buying by prices that were simply too high.

With major banks warning housing values could soften, Mary worries buying today could mean missing the opportunity to secure a bargain tomorrow.

After months of diverging forecasts, Australia’s major banks are increasingly converging around a weaker outlook for housing.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

ANZ now expects capital city house prices to fall 2.1 per cent in 2026, a sharp reversal from its earlier forecast for 2.8 per cent growth, while NAB is forecasting values will decline by around 2 per cent after previously predicting gains.

Westpac has also reported applications for investor housing loans fell 20 per cent in the three weeks following the May budget, another sign changing market conditions may already be influencing buyer behaviour.

But as buyers grow increasingly reluctant amid fears prices could fall further, economists say the key problem for buyers holding off is that the market rarely sends a clear signal that it has reached the bottom.

Tim Lawless, research director at property data company Cotality, told SBS that while many buyers imagine housing cycles as a clean curve, the reality is usually far less obvious.

"Picking the precise peak and trough of the market is probably more a matter of luck than market aptitude," he said.

Instead, he said markets tend to move through periods of gradual change and pointed to Sydney’s recent slowdown as an example, where growth momentum eased before values flattened and then moved into more consistent declines.

Lawless said no single indicator tells the full story and buyers should instead watch for changes across a range of measures, including home values and whether declines are starting to slow, listing volumes and stock levels, auction clearance rates, days on market and vendor discounting.

But independent property economist Cameron Kusher told SBS News that economic indicators often move before prices fully recover, but lower clearance rates and longer selling times can indicate buyers and sellers are becoming further apart on price expectations.

"You’ll probably start to see inflation coming down, stock starting to move and consumer sentiment improving," he said.

Dr Meg Elkins, associate professor in economics at RMIT University, said buyers often focus heavily on avoiding losses, with behavioural economics showing people often fear overpaying more than they value...

body.en:
Child-free life vs child-free world? As more Australians embrace a child-free life, Insight explores why many of us are choosing not to have kids, the stigma that can come with that decision, and the changing face of family. Watch Insight episode No Kids, No Problems? on SBS On Demand.

I've never been able to imagine myself as a mother. I can't pinpoint the exact moment I decided I didn't want children, but I knew from a young age.

Maybe I was born this way, or maybe being the oldest with caring responsibilities in a single-parent household played a role; in some way, I feel I've already parented.

I also watched people around me have kids young and saw what they went through in raising them. If anything, it pushed me further away from wanting that life.

I couldn't relate to people who wanted children, and the idea has always made me uncomfortable.

But there was one time, just over a decade ago, when parenthood was a looming threat.

My period was a few days late, and I had a funny feeling about it, so I took a pregnancy test. It was positive.

I didn't feel excited. It only confirmed what I already felt: I didn't want children.

I didn't hesitate and booked an appointment with the clinic straight away to have an abortion .

I knew I didn't want to go ahead with the pregnancy, and I didn't need time to think about it.

I was uncomfortable in my own body; tired, bloated, nauseous — all of it.

I felt like my body wasn't mine, like a parasite had taken over. That was the hardest part. I just wanted it out of me. There was no connection to it at all.

Relief that my body was mine again. Relief that I had the choice, and I could make that decision for myself.

Proud that I did what was right for me. Proud that I accessed the care I needed.

I've never felt regret — if anything, the whole experience just solidified what I'd always known.

Just over two years ago, I had my fallopian tubes removed — a procedure I had wanted for a long time.

I didn't do it earlier because of doctors' pushback that I'd heard of from family and friends who had been told no — even when they already had children.

But when I finally asked a couple of years ago, I didn't get any pushback at all.

Both my abortion and tubal ligation (which is a permanent form of contraception) were positive experiences in terms of the care I received — and my GP and specialists were supportive.

The tubal ligation was a practical decision; I didn't want to rely on contraception or risk another pregnancy.

I was also diagnosed with endometriosis at the same time, so it was a no-brainer for me.

body.en:
The law is on your side, policy professional Kat George writes. It’s worth making spam and privacy complaints

I made the mistake of giving my email address and phone number to a real estate agent when looking at a property. How do I get random real estate agents I’ve never met to stop harassing me?

Lucky for you, there are two sets of protections in place to help you with this problem. Australia has strict rules and regulations around spam, which mean real estate agents can’t contact you with marketing messages if you don’t want them to. Under Australian privacy laws, they are not allowed to share your personal details with other agents, so you absolutely don’t have to put up with contact from an agent you’ve never met.

Firstly, spam. Under the Spam Act 2003 and the Spam Regulations 2021 , anyone wanting to send you marketing texts or emails must first have your consent. Consent can be either express or inferred.

Express consent is where you give over your details with full knowledge and acceptance that you’re going to receive marketing. For instance, if you’re at an open house and a real estate agent offers to contact you about other listings, or gives you a form to fill out where you tick a box saying you’d like to receive more information, that would be considered express consent.

Inferred consent is where you give over your details and it is reasonable to believe that you expect to receive marketing as a result. For instance, if you give a real estate agent your details at a property inspection, it could arguably be reasonable for them to assume you have consented to being contacted about other properties.

Either way, consent can be withdrawn. Under the spam rules, unsubscribing has to be an easy process for the person receiving marketing messages; every marketing message must contain a clear unsubscribe option; and you must be unsubscribed within five working days when you opt out.

Immediately unsubscribing from all real estate marketing you receive should be your first step. If there is no option to unsubscribe, or you have unsubscribed but are still receiving messages, you should make a complaint to the Australian Communications and Media Authority which can investigate.

It’s worth sharing your issue with Acma either way, as it has authority to investigate systemic issues and take enforcement actions. If the type of issue you’re experiencing happens to be widespread, reporting it can help Acma identify the problem and take appropriate action. Be prepared to provide screenshots of all the communications you have received.

title.en: US military plans major war stockpile on Australian soil
title.zh: 美国军方计划在澳大利亚领土上储存大量战争物资

summary.en: The massive buildup of weapons is part of an Asia-wide regional defence strategy to counter the rise of China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US military is planning a permanent war-ready weapons stockpile for its marine corps on Australia's southeast coast beyond the range of most Chinese missiles, tender documents show and officials confirmed to the Agence France-Presse news agency (AFP).

The development of the stockpile, a first for the US marine corps in Australia, comes as the United States is keen to leverage the continent's strategic location in the South Pacific to counter China's rapid military build-up, analysts said.

The US marine corps began global prepositioning of military supplies during the Cold War — using floating stores on ships and caves in Norway where weapons, ammunition and vehicles to sustain thousands of troops are kept.

The first land stockpile in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to open this year in the Philippines, close to potential flashpoints in the South China Sea.

Documents published by the US navy this month show advanced planning for an even larger Australian stockpile, with US$30 million ($42.4M) allocated to build warehouses and offices in southeastern Victoria state for "critical forward provisioning".

The Australian stockpile, expected to reach full capacity by 2028, will be kept in Melbourne before being moved to US warehouses to be constructed next year at an Australian military base at Bandiana in rural Victoria, tender documents show.

Australia does not permit foreign military bases on its soil, a sensitive issue in a country that has a security alliance with the United States and is hosting an increasing variety of US forces on rotation at Australian defence bases.

The US navy is engaging a global defence contractor to employ around 110 engineers, mechanics, material and safety specialists to manage the Australian stockpile, which includes "crew-served weapons", the documents show.

"Marine corps activities in Australia support integrated global sustainment by maintaining ready-for-issue equipment and supplies for operations and exercises across the Indo-Pacific," a US marine corps forces pacific spokesperson told AFP.

The spokesperson declined to comment on contract details or force planning assumptions but said marines' equipment is kept at "high readiness".

Contracting arrangements and the operation of the facility would be made in close coordination with Australia's Department of Defence.

"These activities improve responsiveness, strengthen interoperability with allies and partners, and support a range of missions across the Indo-Pacific," the spokesperson said, using an alternative description for the Asia-Pacific region.

title.en: Australia's 'deadliest year on record' exposes a worsening hidden crisis
title.zh: 澳大利亚“有记录以来最致命的一年”揭示日益恶化的隐性危机

summary.en: New figures indicate that Australia has reached a somber milestone, marking its deadliest year on record, which highlights a growing and often overlooked crisis within the nation.
summary.zh: 新数据显示，澳大利亚已达到一个悲惨的里程碑，创下有记录以来最致命的一年，这凸显了该国日益恶化且常被忽视的危机。

body.en:
Living in what he described as an "unstable household" and moving from state to state with his parents who also used drugs, it wasn't until he was 15 when visiting a friend he realised his upbringing was not normal.

Now 33, Edgar is an air conditioning and refrigeration mechanic and will mark 12 years in recovery this week. But the toll of drug use has stayed with him: his father, Paul, died from an overdose in 2015.

He said it doesn't surprise him to drug overdoses are killing one person every 3.5 hours in Australia — or an average of seven deaths a day, according to new research from the Melbourne-based Penington Institute.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

A preliminary analysis by the non-profit drug policy research group found some 2,596 Australian died from drug-induced causes in 2024 — what it has described as the "deadliest year on record" for overdoses.

Penington Institute CEO John Ryan told SBS News each drug overdose death is a "tragedy".

"What we’re seeing is [almost] double the number of people dying from overdose than from the road toll and so the scale of the problem is huge," he said.

"It's affecting people from all parts of the country, from all age groups and all socioeconomic backgrounds."

Some 2,091 deaths, or about 80 per cent of the total, were unintentional drug-induced fatalities, according to the preliminary asessment, which will be updated and form part of the group's annual overdose report later this year.

It was the first time the number of unintentional drug-induced deaths had surpassed 2,000, after a jump of about 15 per cent from the year before.

Opioids, including heroin, were the most commonly involved drug type, recorded in 877 unintentional deaths. Deaths involving stimulants, including ice but not cocaine, rose sharply, increasing year-on-year by 25.1 per cent to 772.

Benzodiazepines were the third most commonly involved drug type, recorded in 514 unintentional deaths.

The report noted some deaths are counted in more than one drug category because multiple substances were recorded.

"This premature loss of life is concerning, and it is preventable," said professor Amy Peacock, deputy director of UNSW's National Drug and Alcohol Research Centre, which is not involved with the Penington Institute's report.

"More broadly, we are seeing rising harms related to stimulants such as methamphetamine and cocaine. Globally, we're seeing rising availability of these substances and in Australia … increased hospitalisations and deaths."

title.en: Iraq coach Graham Arnold has achieved something at the World Cup no other Australian has
title.zh: 伊拉克教练格雷厄姆·阿诺德在世界杯上取得了其他澳大利亚人没有取得过的成就

summary.en: Graham Arnold has already proven himself a legend to 46 million Iraqis. How far can he go?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australian coach Graham Arnold has steered Iraq's national team back onto the world stage for the first time in 40 years and their second ever appearance in the tournament.

Such is his hero status that football officials tried to get him citizenship , but the story of how he got there is unexpected.

Arnold is the first Australian coach to take teams to two World Cups, guiding the Socceroos to Qatar in 2022 before switching allegiances.

Over the course of 28 months, with eight spent living in Baghdad, he's taken the squad through an arduous 21 qualifying games complicated by grounded flights out of the Middle East.

On Wednesday morning Australian time, Arnold's Lions of Mesopotamia go head-to-head with Norway in Boston for their first World Cup match in 40 years.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's a long way from Sydney to Baghdad, but for the former Socceroos coach, the team's four-decade drought presented a welcome challenge. As the 62-year-old told Guardian Australia, if it had happened at another time, he may not have done it.

"But the fact that they hadn’t qualified for 40 years was a great challenge. A great opportunity to make 46 million people proud and happy," Arnold said.

In May 2025, Arnold's agent had "randomly" called him with news that Iraq was interested in hiring him. Before then, the former Socceroos manager had been "starting to go crazy, sitting at home staring at four walls" for months.

Arnold told sports podcast The Howie Games his agent had assumed he wouldn't want to take the job. To which he had responded: "Hang on, why?"

As the longest-serving Socceroos manager, Arnold led the team to the World Cup round of 16 in 2022, beating Tunisia and Denmark. It was the furthest the team had made it in the campaign since 2006, and Arnold was the first Australian-born manager to achieve this.

Arnold ended a six-year stint as head Socceroos coach in September 2024 , amid a poor start to the team's World Cup 2026 qualifying matches.

"I resigned for the good of the nation and the players. I didn't want to let the country down because I was cooked," he said.

The timing was fortuitous. The following May, Iraq sacked head coach Jesús Casas after a 2-1 defeat to the Palestinian team in the third round of the Asian confederation World Cup qualifiers. Arnold was given three days to make his decision.

Arriving in Baghdad, Arnold discovered it wasn't just Casas who had been sacked.
